# Downloading with prefetch {#sec-prefetch}

`prefetch` downloads the `.sra` file for a run from NCBI (or from a cloud
copy) to your disk. It isn't strictly required: `fasterq-dump` can stream
directly from NCBI. But downloading first is **much more reliable** for anything
bigger than a test: an interrupted download can resume, you can check the file,
and conversion then needs less temporary space.

## One run

```bash
cd ~/public_data/GSE52778     # any folder with enough free space
prefetch SRR1039508
```

```
2026-11-24T12:00:00 prefetch.3.x: 1) Downloading 'SRR1039508'...
2026-11-24T12:00:00 prefetch.3.x:  Downloading via HTTPS...
2026-11-24T12:03:10 prefetch.3.x:  HTTPS download succeed
2026-11-24T12:03:12 prefetch.3.x:  'SRR1039508' is valid
2026-11-24T12:03:12 prefetch.3.x: 1) 'SRR1039508' was downloaded successfully
```

(Times and version are illustrative.) The result is a **folder named after
the run** with the `.sra` file inside:

```
SRR1039508/
└── SRR1039508.sra       (or SRR1039508.sralite)
```

## Options you'll use

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `-O <dir>` / `--output-directory <dir>` | Put the run folder inside `<dir>` instead of here |
| `-X <size>` / `--max-size <size>` | Size limit. **The default is 20 GB**: bigger runs are skipped with a message. Units `k`, `m`, `g`, `t`, or `u` for unlimited: `--max-size u` |
| `-p` / `--progress` | Show a progress bar |
| `--option-file <file>` | Read accessions from a file, one per line |
| `-f yes` / `--force yes` | Download again even if a copy exists |

```bash
prefetch SRR1039508 -O sra --max-size u -p     # into ./sra/SRR1039508/
```

## Several runs

```bash
cd ~/public_data/GSE52778      # the dataset folder, with SRR_Acc_List.txt in it
prefetch --option-file SRR_Acc_List.txt -O sra --max-size u
## or, equivalently
prefetch $(cat SRR_Acc_List.txt) -O sra --max-size u
```

This downloads one after another. For many runs, split them into an
array job instead ([At scale](at-scale.qmd)).

## How big is it, before I download?

```bash
vdb-dump --info SRR1039508      # includes the size
```

Or use the `Bytes` column of `SraRunTable.csv`.

## Check the download: vdb-validate

`prefetch` checks the file as it finishes (the "is valid" line), but it's
worth checking again before you spend time converting, especially after a
download that was interrupted and resumed:

```bash
vdb-validate sra/SRR1039508
```

It checks every internal checksum and prints `... is consistent` lines; any
`error` or `corrupt` message means delete the folder and `prefetch` again.

::: {.callout-note}
## If a download is interrupted

Run the same `prefetch` command again. It resumes where it stopped and
skips runs that are already complete.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Check your understanding

1. `prefetch` prints "... is larger than maximum allowed: skipped". What do
   you add?
2. Why `cd` into a folder with plenty of space before running `prefetch`?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## Answers

1. `--max-size u` (or a size larger than the run, e.g. `--max-size 100g`).
2. With `--prefetch-to-cwd`, files go to the current folder, and the
   conversion that follows needs 10–20× the download's size free.
:::
:::
